sources.title: Calendars
sources.description: Pick every calendar that can have something {name} needs to be up for: a work calendar, a school or family calendar, a personal one. The next steps ask how to read each.

habits.title: Starting habits
habits.description: Where learning starts for {name}. Each of these is then learned from {name}'s real nights and replaced as they accumulate, so there's no need to come back and adjust them.

data.free_bedtime: Usual bedtime with no shift nearby

data_description.free_bedtime: On nights with nothing early the next morning.
data_description.target_sleep_hours: Before a shift that gets {name} up.
data_description.wind_down_minutes: How early the Wind-down sensor turns on, for dimming lights or cooling the bedroom. This one is a preference, not learned.

signals.title: How to tell when {name} sleeps
signals.description: Pick at least one signal. Use as many as you have: when one is missing (a watch not worn, a flaky sensor), the others fill in.

data_description.in_bed_signals: On while {name} is in bed: a bed pressure sensor for their side, an mmWave presence sensor aimed at the bed, or similar. 20 minutes settled counts as going to sleep; 3 hours or more counts as a night.
data_description.asleep_signals: Measured sleep, such as Sleep as Android, Withings, Fitbit, or Apple Health sleep data (e.g. via Health Auto Export). Trusted straight away. Not Sleep Focus or bedtime schedules: those follow preset times, not actual sleep.
data_description.asleep_states: Only matters for trackers that report text states. Any of these states counts as asleep.

learning.title: Learning and feedback
learning.description: All optional. Nights that are not typical for {name} (guests, travel, illness) can be kept out of learning.

data.notify_service: Send a note after each night to

data_description.pause_entities: For example a home-mode selector or a guest/vacation toggle. Nights are not learned while any of these is in one of the states below. There is also a Learning switch to pause by hand.
data_description.pause_states: Matched ignoring case. Type your own and press Enter to add it.
data_description.notify_service: A phone from the Home Assistant app. After each recorded night it gets a note with a Forget button, for nights that were not normal.
data_description.use_sleep_debt: Also compare how much {name} slept in the previous 48 hours, since short nights tend to lead to earlier bedtimes. Best turned on once a few weeks of nights have been learned.

person.title: Who is this for?
person.description:
Predictive Sleep learns when someone goes to sleep from their work schedule and their bed, then predicts upcoming bedtimes so the home can get ready ahead of time.

Add one entry per person.

user.title: Predictive Sleep
user.description:
Predictive Sleep learns when each person goes to sleep from their work schedule and sleep signals, then predicts upcoming bedtimes so the home can get ready ahead of time.

Predictive Sleep v{version} by Goobis
AI was used to help develop this integration.

household.title: Household sensors
household.description: Adds whole-home sensors across everyone set up: whether everyone home is expected asleep, whether anyone is winding down, and the earliest and latest predicted bedtimes. Useful for locks, heating and common-area lights, especially without a home-mode system of your own.

calendar.title: Reading {calendar}
calendar.description: Tell Predictive Sleep which events on {calendar} mean {name} needs to be up. All-day events (birthdays, holidays) are always ignored.

data_description.mode: Work shifts shape the whole sleep pattern. On a mixed calendar only events with the words below count, and those that are not work are treated as appointments: they set how early {name} must be up, nothing more.
data_description.words: Whole words, ignoring case: "doctor" matches "Doctor (Sam)" and "Sam doctor", not "Doctors' Day party". Type your own and press Enter. Ignored for work calendars.
data_description.require_name: For calendars shared with others, e.g. "{name} dentist" counts but "Alex dentist" does not. Home Assistant can't see who created an event, so the name in the title or description stands in for it.

error.no_signals: Pick at least one in-bed signal or sleep tracker.

abort.already_configured: This person is already set up.
abort.household_exists: Household sensors are already set up.

settings.title: Sleep signals, learning and habits

data.settle_minutes: Time in bed before it counts as a sleep attempt
data.wake_gap_minutes: Time out of bed before it counts as awake
data.min_sleep_hours: Shortest stretch that counts as a night
data.notify_service: Send a note after each night to

data_description.learning_window_days: Nights older than this are discarded. Within the window, recent nights count more.
data_description.asleep_states: Only matters for trackers that report text states.
data_description.use_sleep_debt: Also compare how much was slept in the previous 48 hours.

settings.description: Usual bedtime, sleep needed, get-ready and unwind time aren't here: they're learned from real nights. The values given at setup were only the starting point.

error.no_signals: Pick at least one in-bed signal or sleep tracker.

forget_last_night.name: Forget last sleep
forget_last_night.description: Removes the most recently recorded sleep from learning, for one that was not typical.

entry_not_loaded.message: That Predictive Sleep entry is not loaded.

missing_calendar.title: {name}: calendar not found
missing_calendar.description: Predictive Sleep can't find {calendars}. It may have been removed or renamed, so {name}'s predictions are using the last shifts it read. Choose the calendars again under Settings → Devices & services → Predictive Sleep → Configure → Calendars.
